# SECOND RUN REBUILD MASTER PROMPT: RESURRECTING PRISMSCALE
# INDUSTRY: EDTECH & LEARNING · CAPITAL BURNED: $16.5M · BATCH: W20
# TARGET AGENTS: Cursor Composer / Windsurf Cascade / Claude Code / Aider
# PURPOSE: Rebuild the core value proposition of PrismScale to the absolute limits
#          while strictly enforcing the "Anti-Death" negative engineering rules.
# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "PrismScale" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: PrismScale
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $16.5M
- Target Sector: EdTech & Learning
- YC Batch: W20

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual EdTech & Learning overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original PrismScale raised $16.5M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Attempted to fulfill software promises through behind-the-scenes human services. Customer acquisition cost outstripped lifetime value, leading to fatal unit burn when venture funding tightened."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Hiring human service specialists before achieving true software automation.
2. Subsidizing operational labor deficits with venture equity.
3. Failing to enforce standard self-serve checkout.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When PrismScale died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as a 100% autonomous serverless micro-SaaS with zero human service bottlenecks, sub-5-cent marginal compute, and instant 60-second time-to-value.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Self-serve flat subscription at $49/mo with 92% gross margins.

# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "AtlasFlow" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: AtlasFlow
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $38.0M
- Target Sector: HealthTech & Biometrics
- YC Batch: S19

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual HealthTech & Biometrics overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original AtlasFlow raised $38.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Attempted to fulfill software promises through behind-the-scenes human services. Customer acquisition cost outstripped lifetime value, leading to fatal unit burn when venture funding tightened."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Hiring human service specialists before achieving true software automation.
2. Subsidizing operational labor deficits with venture equity.
3. Failing to enforce standard self-serve checkout.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When AtlasFlow died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as a 100% autonomous serverless micro-SaaS with zero human service bottlenecks, sub-5-cent marginal compute, and instant 60-second time-to-value.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Self-serve flat subscription at $49/mo with 92% gross margins.

# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "CognitoStack" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: CognitoStack
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $52.0M
- Target Sector: E-Commerce & Retail
- YC Batch: S19

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual E-Commerce & Retail overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original CognitoStack raised $52.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Built a venture-backed tool on host platform APIs without owning the customer relationship or identity layer. When the platform updated its terms or introduced native features, demand evaporated."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Building core value entirely within an un-owned third-party walled garden.
2. Neglecting to build proprietary data moats or direct audience channels.
3. Ignoring platform developer terms warnings until accounts were suspended.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When CognitoStack died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as an open-source, self-hosted developer protocol with multi-platform webhook adapters and zero vendor lock-in.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Open-core model: free open-source engine + $79/mo hosted multi-tenant cloud sync.

name: Fast
tagline: Universal 1-click checkout button designed to eliminate checkout forms and cart abandonment across independent web storefronts.
fatalFlawSummary: Burned $10M/month with 400 employees while generating only $600k in annual revenue trying to build 1-click checkout.

teardown.overview:
Fast offered a universal, one-click checkout button for independent ecommerce merchants. Rather than forcing shoppers to fill out 14 form fields (shipping address, billing address, credit card numbers, password creation) on every new website, Fast remembered user credentials across the entire web. A shopper clicking 'Fast Checkout' bought the product instantly in less than 2 seconds.

Cart abandonment is a trillion-dollar pain point for merchants. Fast raised $124M led by Stripe and Index Ventures on the promise of dethroning Amazon's 1-click checkout patent. The tech world buzzed with excitement as Fast's charismatic CEO Domm Holland promised to make independent ecommerce faster than Amazon.
teardown.fatalFlaw: Hyper-inflated team growth and splashy marketing sponsorships (NASCAR, sports stadiums) with virtually zero organic merchant adoption. Shop Pay already solved 1-click checkout for 80% of merchants.
antiPatterns: Spending millions on consumer brand sponsorships for a B2B infrastructure product.
Hiring 400+ employees before proving merchant distribution or repeat transaction volume.
Ignoring incumbent platform lock-in (Shopify's Shop Pay monopoly on checkout).

# PURPOSE: Rebuild the core value proposition of KryptonMetrics to the absolute limits
#          while strictly enforcing the "Anti-Death" negative engineering rules.
# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "KryptonMetrics" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: KryptonMetrics
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $52.0M
- Target Sector: Developer Tools
- YC Batch: W19

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual Developer Tools overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original KryptonMetrics raised $52.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Hired 25 field sales reps and enterprise account executives before proving organic buyer demand. The 9-to-14 month enterprise procurement timelines bled cash reserves dry before deals closed."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Building a heavy field sales team before achieving product-market fit.
2. Accommodating bespoke custom enterprise feature requests that fragmented the codebase.
3. Ignoring self-serve product-led growth in favor of lengthy RFP tenders.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When KryptonMetrics died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as a bottom-up developer tool with frictionless self-serve onboarding, transparent public pricing, and zero sales calls.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Self-serve pricing: $49/mo Starter, $149/mo Team tier with instant 1-click credit card activation.

# TARGET AGENTS: Cursor Composer / Windsurf Cascade / Claude Code / Aider
# PURPOSE: Rebuild the core value proposition of CipherMesh Cloud to the absolute limits
#          while strictly enforcing the "Anti-Death" negative engineering rules.
# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "CipherMesh Cloud" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: CipherMesh Cloud
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $12.0M
- Target Sector: Developer Tools
- YC Batch: W18

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual Developer Tools overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original CipherMesh Cloud raised $12.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Built a venture-backed tool on host platform APIs without owning the customer relationship or identity layer. When the platform updated its terms or introduced native features, demand evaporated."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Building core value entirely within an un-owned third-party walled garden.
2. Neglecting to build proprietary data moats or direct audience channels.
3. Ignoring platform developer terms warnings until accounts were suspended.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When CipherMesh Cloud died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as an open-source, self-hosted developer protocol with multi-platform webhook adapters and zero vendor lock-in.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Open-core model: free open-source engine + $79/mo hosted multi-tenant cloud sync.

# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "HelixTrack Labs" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: HelixTrack Labs
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $75.0M
- Target Sector: Fintech & Payments
- YC Batch: S18

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual Fintech & Payments overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original HelixTrack Labs raised $75.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Built a venture-backed tool on host platform APIs without owning the customer relationship or identity layer. When the platform updated its terms or introduced native features, demand evaporated."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Building core value entirely within an un-owned third-party walled garden.
2. Neglecting to build proprietary data moats or direct audience channels.
3. Ignoring platform developer terms warnings until accounts were suspended.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When HelixTrack Labs died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as an open-source, self-hosted developer protocol with multi-platform webhook adapters and zero vendor lock-in.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================

==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.

  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Open-core model: free open-source engine + $79/mo hosted multi-tenant cloud sync.

# SECOND RUN REBUILD MASTER PROMPT: RESURRECTING APEXMESH
# INDUSTRY: HR & RECRUITING · CAPITAL BURNED: $12.0M · BATCH: S17
# TARGET AGENTS: Cursor Composer / Windsurf Cascade / Claude Code / Aider
# PURPOSE: Rebuild the core value proposition of ApexMesh to the absolute limits
#          while strictly enforcing the "Anti-Death" negative engineering rules.
# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "ApexMesh" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: ApexMesh
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $12.0M
- Target Sector: HR & Recruiting
- YC Batch: S17

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual HR & Recruiting overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original ApexMesh raised $12.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Suffered negative unit contribution margins on every fulfilled customer order. Management believed volume would produce supplier discounts, but fixed operational overhead compounded losses."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Selling physical units or deliveries below true marginal fulfillment cost.
2. Signing multi-year commercial warehouse leases ahead of stable repeat cohort retention.
3. Counting speculative pre-orders as realized enterprise revenue.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When ApexMesh died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as a zero-inventory digital orchestration SaaS licensing routing and inventory algorithms directly to existing regional operators.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: B2B SaaS: $99/mo per regional operator plus $0.05 per routed delivery.

name: Atrium
tagline: Full-service corporate law firm powered by machine learning to automate startup legal paperwork, SAFEs, and fundraising docs.
fatalFlawSummary: Attempted to disrupt corporate legal services by hiring 100+ high-salary partners while building software that lawyers refused to adopt.

teardown.overview:
Atrium promised founders an end to the archaic $1,000/hour billable attorney model. Justin Kan (co-founder of Twitch) launched Atrium to provide venture-backed startups with transparent, flat-rate legal services powered by proprietary machine-learning software. The platform automated standard corporate documents—incorporation paperwork, standard SAFE agreements, commercial NDAs, and equity cap tables—giving founders on-demand legal counsel without the fear of an unpredictable invoice at month-end.

With Justin Kan's celebrity founder status, Atrium instantly attracted $75.5M from Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, and General Catalyst. Over 250 high-growth startups signed up in their first year, treating Atrium as their de-facto general counsel. Clients loved the modern interface, instantaneous SAFE generation, and fixed-price transparency.
teardown.fatalFlaw: Tried to be both a tech software company and a licensed law firm. Software development could not keep pace with the massive salaried burn of corporate attorneys who preferred Microsoft Word and billable hours.
antiPatterns: Hiring high-salary service specialists before software workflows were automated.
Fighting industry structural incentives (billable hours vs. software efficiency).
Scaling team headcount to 200+ employees on speculative software productivity gains.

teardown.agentPrompt:
ROLE: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
GOAL: Build MVP of Atrium 2.0 (Legal Ops SaaS)
STACK: Next.js 14 (App Router), Prisma, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HelloSign API

SPEC:
1. User Authentication via NextAuth (Google/Email)
2. Document Generation Engine using predefined templates
3. Signature Request Workflow via HelloSign
4. Payment Integration via Stripe Checkout
5. Audit Logging for all document actions

ARCHITECTURE SEAMS (PRISMA SCHEMA):
model User {
  id            String    @id @default(uuid())
  email         String    @unique
  name          String?
  stripeCustomerId String?
  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
  documents     LegalDocument[]
}

model Startup {
  id            String    @id @default(uuid())
  name          String
  state         String
  userId        String
  user          User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  documents     LegalDocument[]
}

model LegalDocument {
  id            String    @id @default(uuid())
  type          String    @default("SAFE")
  status        String    @default("DRAFT")
  contentUrl    String?
  startupId     String
  startup       Startup   @relation(fields: [startupId], references: [id])
  signatureRequests SignatureRequest[]
  auditLogs     AuditLog[]
}

model SignatureRequest {
  id            String    @id @default(uuid())
  helloSignId   String    @unique
  status        String    @default("PENDING")
  documentId    String
  document      LegalDocument @relation(fields: [documentId], references: [id])
}

model AuditLog {
  id            String    @id @default(uuid())
  action        String
  timestamp     DateTime  @default(now())
  documentId    String
  document      LegalDocument @relation(fields: [documentId], references: [id])
}

TO-TICKETS (IMPLEMENTATION PLAN):
1. [SETUP] Initialize Next.js 14 repo with TypeScript, Tailwind, and install Prisma. Configure .env for Database URL and Stripe/HelloSign keys.
2. [DB] Define schema.prisma with models above. Run migrations. Seed one test User and Startup.
3. [AUTH] Implement NextAuth with Google Provider. Protect /dashboard route. Link User to Stripe Customer on first login.
4. [CORE] Build API route /api/generate-document accepting template type. Use pdf-lib or similar to populate template. Save record to LegalDocument table.
5. [SIGN] Integrate HelloSign API. Create signature request upon document finalization. Webhook handler to update SignatureRequest status to 'SIGNED'.

The original ByteScale Labs raised $16.5M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Built a venture-backed tool on host platform APIs without owning the customer relationship or identity layer. When the platform updated its terms or introduced native features, demand evaporated."

When ByteScale Labs died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
- Company: KryptonFlow AI

- Target Sector: Gig Economy & Logistics

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original KryptonFlow AI raised $1.2M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Hired 25 field sales reps and enterprise account executives before proving organic buyer demand. The 9-to-14 month enterprise procurement timelines bled cash reserves dry before deals closed."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Building a heavy field sales team before achieving product-market fit.
2. Accommodating bespoke custom enterprise feature requests that fragmented the codebase.
3. Ignoring self-serve product-led growth in favor of lengthy RFP tenders.

==============================================================================

==============================================================================
When KryptonFlow AI died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

name: LunchBadger
tagline: Visual microservices composition platform enabling backend developers to visually design and deploy serverless APIs on Kubernetes.
fatalFlawSummary: Complex Kubernetes API microservices gateway was too heavyweight for solo devs and too unproven for Fortune 500 CIOs.

teardown.overview:
LunchBadger provided backend engineers with a visual canvas to wire together Express gateways, serverless functions, and database connectors on Kubernetes without writing hundreds of lines of boilerplate YAML.

Backed by YC W18, LunchBadger caught the crest of the enterprise microservices migration, helping DevOps teams visualize and orchestrate distributed cloud infrastructure.
teardown.fatalFlaw: Caught in the enterprise developer tool chasm: too complex for individual engineers to install self-serve, but lacked the enterprise security compliance and brand authority to win six-figure enterprise contracts.
antiPatterns: Building an enterprise developer product without a bottom-up open-source adoption wedge.
Targeting complex Kubernetes orchestration before cloud managed services matured.
Long 9-month sales cycles that drained runway with small average deal sizes.

# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "TandemMetrics" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: TandemMetrics
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $110.0M
- Target Sector: Fintech & Payments
- YC Batch: S17

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual Fintech & Payments overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original TandemMetrics raised $110.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Attempted to fulfill software promises through behind-the-scenes human services. Customer acquisition cost outstripped lifetime value, leading to fatal unit burn when venture funding tightened."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Hiring human service specialists before achieving true software automation.
2. Subsidizing operational labor deficits with venture equity.
3. Failing to enforce standard self-serve checkout.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When TandemMetrics died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as a 100% autonomous serverless micro-SaaS with zero human service bottlenecks, sub-5-cent marginal compute, and instant 60-second time-to-value.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Self-serve flat subscription at $49/mo with 92% gross margins.

==============================================================================
- Company: AuraPoint
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $1.2M
- Target Sector: HealthTech & Biometrics
- YC Batch: S16

The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual HealthTech & Biometrics overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original AuraPoint raised $1.2M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Suffered negative unit contribution margins on every fulfilled customer order. Management believed volume would produce supplier discounts, but fixed operational overhead compounded losses."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Selling physical units or deliveries below true marginal fulfillment cost.
2. Signing multi-year commercial warehouse leases ahead of stable repeat cohort retention.
3. Counting speculative pre-orders as realized enterprise revenue.

==============================================================================
When AuraPoint died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: StackPoint Data

==============================================================================
The original StackPoint Data raised $38.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Attempted to fulfill software promises through behind-the-scenes human services. Customer acquisition cost outstripped lifetime value, leading to fatal unit burn when venture funding tightened."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Hiring human service specialists before achieving true software automation.
2. Subsidizing operational labor deficits with venture equity.
3. Failing to enforce standard self-serve checkout.

When StackPoint Data died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

# INDUSTRY: B2B SAAS · CAPITAL BURNED: $24.0M · BATCH: W15
# TARGET AGENTS: Cursor Composer / Windsurf Cascade / Claude Code / Aider
# PURPOSE: Rebuild the core value proposition of AtlasLogic Cloud to the absolute limits
#          while strictly enforcing the "Anti-Death" negative engineering rules.
# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "AtlasLogic Cloud" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: AtlasLogic Cloud
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $24.0M
- Target Sector: B2B SaaS
- YC Batch: W15

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual B2B SaaS overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original AtlasLogic Cloud raised $24.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Launched in a highly regulated sector without adequate compliance armor or clear licensing. State regulators and industry incumbents launched devastating legal proceedings that consumed all working capital."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Treating regulated consumer sectors like unregulated social software.
2. Ignoring statutory licensing requirements until served with cease-and-desist orders.
3. Spending more on legal defense retainers than engineering development.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When AtlasLogic Cloud died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as a pure analytical and diagnostic productivity tool operating completely outside regulatory scope with clear disclaimers.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Productivity SaaS: $39/mo flat with complete liability disclaimers and zero bespoke professional advice.

sections.title: The Origin, The Promise & What They Built
sections.body:
Eden gave office managers a unified operating system for physical workplaces. Instead of juggling 12 different vendors, Eden provided a single dashboard to manage janitorial cleaning, plumbing, HVAC maintenance, IT wiring, and kitchen snack inventory.

Eden raised $40M from Y Combinator and Bessemer, managing thousands of startup and corporate headquarters across San Francisco, New York, and Austin.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Eden (YC Summer 2015) bundled office services into a single subscription layer. Customers booked vetted providers for cleaning, pantry, repairs, and support tickets, while Eden handled billing and quality control. The buyer was the office manager, and the promise was hours saved every week.

sections.title: Post-Mortem
sections.body: Services marketplaces carry supply-side risk: quality varies by city, margins compress as providers multi-home, and the 2020 shift to remote work removed the office itself for many customers. Consolidation into a larger facilities platform was the viable exit once standalone growth slowed.

sections.title: Key Lessons
sections.body: Managed marketplaces must own either demand aggregation at scale or the supply side (employed staff, not contractors). A thin coordination layer over third-party vendors is hard to defend when a large buyer can replicate the vendor list.

fatalFlawSummary: Self-driving truck pioneer ran out of capital because venture investors shifted from self-driving hardware to AI software.

teardown.overview:
Starsky Robotics took a radically practical approach to autonomous freight: remove the driver entirely from the cab. Self-driving algorithms drove the 80,000 lb semi-truck on straight highways, while remote human tele-operators in an office navigated complex depot yards using steering wheels and monitors.

In 2019, Starsky became the first company in history to drive a fully unmanned 18-wheeler semi-truck on an active public highway with no human in the vehicle. They raised $20M and logged real freight revenue with Fortune 500 shippers.

## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: SyncVault

- Target Sector: LegalTech & Compliance

Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original SyncVault raised $12.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Hired 25 field sales reps and enterprise account executives before proving organic buyer demand. The 9-to-14 month enterprise procurement timelines bled cash reserves dry before deals closed."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Building a heavy field sales team before achieving product-market fit.
2. Accommodating bespoke custom enterprise feature requests that fragmented the codebase.
3. Ignoring self-serve product-led growth in favor of lengthy RFP tenders.

When SyncVault died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

==============================================================================
- Company: Zume Pizza
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $445.0M
- Target Sector: Hardware & IoT
- YC Batch: W16

The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.

Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original Zume Pizza raised $445.0M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Robotic pizza assembly was prone to sauce splatters, melted cheese shifts around road corners, and constant kitchen robot recalibrations. The custom delivery trucks cost hundreds of thousands of dollars each and suffered frequent mechanical breakdowns."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Attempting to solve food service economics by moving heavy industrial robotics inside delivery vehicles.
2. Accepting mega-checks ($375M SoftBank) that forced unnatural expansion into compostable packaging before unit economics worked.
3. Ignoring traditional commercial kitchen equipment that was 50x cheaper and more reliable.

==============================================================================

==============================================================================
When Zume Pizza died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as an automated predictive inventory and prep-scheduling SaaS for existing independent pizzerias based on local weather and event webhooks.

- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Pure software SaaS: $89/mo per pizzeria location with zero hardware liability.

tagline: Hourly staff hiring and onboarding platform using video cover letters and text messages to staff restaurant and retail franchises.
fatalFlawSummary: High customer churn among franchise restaurant owners due to enterprise sales cycles and heavy manual phone screening.

teardown.overview:
HigherMe targeted the high-turnover restaurant and retail labor market. Instead of paper applications, candidates applied through automated text messages and 30-second video snippets. Franchisees could review, score, and schedule interviews in seconds from their phones.

Founded by a former multi-unit franchise owner, HigherMe won YC W15 backing. Franchise giants including Dunkin' Donuts, Panera Bread, and Domino's adopted the platform, reducing time-to-hire by over 65% for thousands of restaurant managers.
teardown.fatalFlaw: Selling enterprise applicant tracking software into franchise operators required high-friction field sales reps, while turnover in retail/restaurant labor caused severe account churn.
antiPatterns: Relying on field sales reps to close small franchise retail owners with low ACVs.
Building heavy desktop-first hiring portals for mobile-first hourly restaurant workers.
Neglecting automated SMS interview scheduling in early iterations.

The original LoomMetrics raised $16.5M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

When LoomMetrics died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

# ============================================================================
# SECOND RUN REBUILD MASTER PROMPT: RESURRECTING OPTICSHIELD
# INDUSTRY: DEVELOPER TOOLS · CAPITAL BURNED: $8.5M · BATCH: S14
# TARGET AGENTS: Cursor Composer / Windsurf Cascade / Claude Code / Aider
# PURPOSE: Rebuild the core value proposition of OpticShield to the absolute limits
#          while strictly enforcing the "Anti-Death" negative engineering rules.
# ============================================================================

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
Your mission is to rebuild "OpticShield" from scratch in this workspace as a 100% automated, zero-human-headcount micro-SaaS.

==============================================================================
## § 1. TARGET IDENTITY & VALIDATED MARKET DEMAND
==============================================================================
- Company: OpticShield
- Total Venture Capital Burned: $8.5M
- Target Sector: Developer Tools
- YC Batch: S14

### Why the Market Demand is 100% Real:
The original company did NOT die from lack of customer demand. They had passionate early adopters, significant waitlists, and validated willingness-to-pay.
The underlying customer pain point—eliminating expensive, slow, and manual Developer Tools overhead—remains completely unsolved for early-stage teams and growing businesses.
Customers are currently desperate for an affordable, transparent, self-serve alternative and are overpaying legacy incumbents.

==============================================================================
## § 2. THE FORENSIC AUTOPSY: HOW THEY KILLED IT (THE DEATH TRAP)
==============================================================================
The original OpticShield raised $8.5M and collapsed due to the following fatal failure mechanics:

### The Fatal Flaw:
"Built a venture-backed tool on host platform APIs without owning the customer relationship or identity layer. When the platform updated its terms or introduced native features, demand evaporated."

### The CAC vs. LTV Inversion:
1. They hired expensive human specialists, practitioners, and sales reps to perform bespoke services disguised as software.
2. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) exploded past sustainable limits because they relied on outbound sales calls, custom demos, and high-touch account management.
3. Payback periods stretched beyond 14 months. When venture capital market conditions shifted, their burn rate wiped them out.

### The 3 Fatal Anti-Patterns They Fell Into:
1. Building core value entirely within an un-owned third-party walled garden.
2. Neglecting to build proprietary data moats or direct audience channels.
3. Ignoring platform developer terms warnings until accounts were suspended.

==============================================================================
## § 3. IN-DEPTH COMPETITOR STUDY & THE VULNERABILITY MATRIX
==============================================================================
When OpticShield died, legacy incumbents monopolized the market by gouging customers with opaque enterprise contracts.

### Competitor Vulnerability Audit (Why Customers Hate Them):
- Price Gouging: Incumbents charge thousands per year or bill per transaction with opaque enterprise tiers.
- Legacy Technical Debt: Most incumbent software was built 8–12 years ago with slow page loads and complex configuration menus.
- Gated Access: Forcing prospects through "Schedule a Demo with Sales" forms instead of allowing them to test the product immediately.

### The Asymmetric Attack Wedge:
- Attack Wedge: Rebuild as an open-source, self-hosted developer protocol with multi-platform webhook adapters and zero vendor lock-in.
- Why Customers Will Switch: Instant self-serve setup in 60 seconds, transparent $49/mo flat billing, zero sales reps, and modern AI automation.

==============================================================================
## § 4. "ANTI-DEATH" NEGATIVE ENGINEERING GUARDRAILS (WHAT THE AGENT MUST NEVER BUILD)
==============================================================================
As the AI coding agent building this product, you MUST obey these non-negotiable negative constraints:

- RULE 1: ZERO HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP SERVICE HEADCOUNT.
  Under NO circumstances should you build internal admin tools for human service workers, consultant booking calendars, or manual approval queues. If a workflow cannot be resolved in code or via automated LLM reasoning, DO NOT BUILD IT.

- RULE 2: FIXED MARGINAL COMPUTE COST (< $0.05 PER TRANSACTION).
  The predecessor burned hundreds of dollars in human labor per customer request. Our total marginal compute cost (LLM tokens, database read/write, edge execution) must stay strictly under 5 cents per run.

- RULE 3: 100% SELF-SERVE TIME-TO-VALUE (< 60 SECONDS).
  Never implement a "Contact Sales to Activate" wall. A new user must be able to authenticate, configure their parameters, and view their first live automated output in less than 60 seconds.

- RULE 4: MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION WITH ZERO LEAKAGE.
  Every query must enforce strict organization boundary scoping: where: { organizationId: session.user.orgId }. No shared memory or cross-tenant leaks.

==============================================================================
## § 5. THE 2026 CIRCUMVENTION ARCHITECTURE & COMPLETE PRISMA SCHEMA
==============================================================================
- Framework: Next.js 14 App Router (Server Actions, Route Handlers, Edge Middleware)
- Database: PostgreSQL / SQLite with Prisma ORM
- Auth: NextAuth.js (Auth.js v5) with Multi-Tenant Organization Isolation
- Payments: Stripe Billing ($49/mo Starter, $149/mo Growth) with idempotent HMAC webhooks
- Unit Economics: Open-core model: free open-source engine + $79/mo hosted multi-tenant cloud sync.

name: ScaleFactor
tagline: Autonomous bookkeeping and financial intelligence platform promising to automate accounting for small businesses without CPAs.
fatalFlawSummary: Promised automated AI bookkeeping to small businesses, but secretly used offshore human accountants in the Philippines who made catastrophic ledger errors.

teardown.overview:
ScaleFactor promised small business owners a complete 'autonomous finance department'. Instead of paying thousands to traditional CPAs or wrestling with complex QuickBooks entries, business owners connected their bank accounts to ScaleFactor's AI engine. The software promised to categorize transactions, reconcile bank accounts, produce P&L statements, and file taxes automatically with zero human friction.

ScaleFactor raised $100M from Bessemer Venture Partners, Canaan, and Coatue, growing at a blistering pace across Austin and the US. Small business owners were eager to offload the headache of manual bookkeeping to a self-driving software platform.
teardown.fatalFlaw: Sold prospective venture capitalists and clients on proprietary AI accounting software that did not exist. Behind the scenes, outsourced human bookkeepers worked frantically in spreadsheets, misclassifying thousands of client transactions.
antiPatterns: Selling AI automation before having functional deterministic software.
Faking software capabilities with hidden, unscalable offshore labor.
Prioritizing hyper-growth sales commissions over client audit accuracy.

name: Secret
tagline: Anonymous social network for Silicon Valley tech insiders to share unfiltered confessions, leaks, and candid workplace discussions.
fatalFlawSummary: Toxicity, cyberbullying, and unmoderated gossip destroyed retention once early Silicon Valley curiosity faded.

teardown.overview:
Secret allowed users to post short messages and photos completely anonymously, which were distributed strictly to contacts in their address book and their friends-of-friends. teardown.overview:
Teforia was the Nespresso of gourmet tea. Engineered by ex-Xbox designer Allen Han, the gorgeous glass-and-bamboo machine used optical scanners and micro-infusion algorithms to optimize water temperature, steep time, and aeration for rare loose-leaf tea varietals.

You are a Principal Software Architect, Forensic Startup Auditor, and Autonomous Venture Builder.
